newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan auto body sees no big rise in future exports.
newsitem.headline: Japan auto body sees no big rise in future exports.

text.p: Japan's car exports jumped more than 30 percent in June, but an industry body said on Monday that the sharp increase was unlikely to carry over into the second half of this year.

Exports in June rose 31.9 percent from a year earlier to 418,137 units, pushing exports for the January-June period to 2.18 million units, up 20.6 percent from a year ago, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association said on Monday.
But an association official said even though it was the first time exports had increased in the first half of the year since the first half of 1992, that the growth was unlikely to persist.

"Exports are unlikely to continue their sharp growth in the second half of this year because of uncertainty about future moves in the U.S. car market, and because exports were comparatively high in the second half of last year," an association official said.

Exports to the United States rose 22.3 percent in the January-June period from the year-earlier period to 634,394 units, the first time they had increased in the first half year period since the first half of 1986, helped by the weaker yen.
"The growth rate for January-June appears high, but that just stems from poor exports last year. The actual volume this year was about the same as in the first half of 1995," the official said.

Seiji Sugiura, an industry analyst of Nomura Securities Co Ltd's research unit, also said exports were likely to start falling later this year because of worries of possible trade friction with the United States, and to keep overseas inventories at proper levels.
Sugiura said he expects a seven percent decline in the October-December period after a gain of seven percent in the July-September period.
He estimated that Japan's exports for all of 1997 would reach 4.15 million units, up 12 percent from a year earlier.
Toyota Motor Corp does not plan a change in its projected exports of 1.33 million units this year, up 4.0 percent from 1996, a Toyota spokesman said.
Toyota's exports in the January-June period were up 12.4 percent from a year earlier to 703,458 units, the manufacturers' association said.
Last week, Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda said Toyota's exports to the United States in 1997 were expected to be unchanged to five percent higher compared to last year.
"We have yet to decide on export levels in the second half," a Nissan Motor Co Ltd spokesman said. "We may curb exports in the latter half to avoid possible trade friction."
Nissan earlier projected its calendar 1997 exports at 600,000 units, up 3.3 percent from a year earlier. The association said Nissan's exports for January to June were up 21.1 percent to 331,954.

Honda Motor Co Ltd also said it has no plans to change its export plans for 1997, with overall exports projected at 470,000 cars, up 15.1 percent from a year earlier. That includes exports of 240,000 cars to the United States, up from 151,633 in 1996.
